events.did: asked Eli whether the moniker or the ability came first and whether Eli willed it into being
events.quote_anchor: “I’m curious, which came first, the moniker or the ability? Eli Ever. Ever, as in immortal. Did you know what you’d become? Did you will it into being?”

events.did: said he and Victor had a theory that determination played a part
events.quote_anchor: “We had a theory,” he said. “That determination played a part.”

events.did: told Eli he honestly did not know where Victor was
events.quote_anchor: Gabriel shook his head. “I honestly don’t know.”

events.did: showed Eli on a tablet the grid of videos from EON’s cells and pointed out Mr. Vale was not among the current patients
events.quote_anchor: “EON’s current patients. As you can see, Mr. Vale is not among them.”

events.did: explained they did find Victor everywhere because someone coded him into the surveillance with false leads, dead ends and booby traps
events.quote_anchor: Gabriel explained it wasn’t that they couldn’t find him. It was that they found him everywhere.

events.did: named the theory “Cognitive emphasis,” saying that under extreme duress the subject’s determination played a part, and surrendered the tablet
events.quote_anchor: “Cognitive emphasis,” he said, finally surrendering the device, which vanished into the chair at Gabriel’s side.

events.did: described going into the ice bath knowing what he wanted and holding on to being unstoppable, unbreakable and unkillable
events.quote_anchor: I wanted to be unstoppable. Unbreakable. Unkillable. I held on to it like a rope.

events.did: told Gabriel he resents him, but not because he is an EO, rather because he is not God
events.quote_anchor: Eli met his eyes. “No, Gabriel,” he said. “Because you’re not God.”

relations.quote_anchor: “Do you resent me for resurrecting you?” asked Gabriel.

relations.did: has hunted Victor for two and a half years and holds Gabriel responsible for failing to catch him
relations.quote_anchor: “Two and a half years is a long time,” countered Eli. “You should have caught him. You could have caught him. He could be here.”

relations.did: brings EOs back, and every EO he has brought back has presented glitches
relations.quote_anchor: “Glitches are inevitable. They’ve presented in every single EO I’ve brought back. Trust me when I say, yours could be far worse.”
“Mitchell Turner,” muttered Eli, recalling the troublesome cellmate.

numbers.who: the clock on the wall of Gabriel’s office
numbers.quote_anchor: the clock on the wall of Gabriel’s office, which now read half past three.

numbers.did: has been missing for Two and a half years
numbers.quote_anchor: “Two and a half years is a long time,” countered Eli.

numbers.who: the tablet footage of EON’s cells
numbers.did: came from a dozen cells that looked identical to Eli’s
numbers.quote_anchor: On the screen, a grid of videos—footage from a dozen cells that looked identical to his.

numbers.who: the cell footage on the tablet
numbers.quote_anchor: Three were empty. The others contained figures who sat, or stood, rested, paced.
